title: Localization of an oriented product at a representable triple
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be the left oriented product on the triple site of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. For a triple $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$, let $H_Z=h_Z^\#$ be the associated representable sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Then there is a canonical equivalence over $P$
$$P/H_Z\simeq U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{V_{\mathrm{Et}}}W_{\mathrm{Et}},$$
where the maps to $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$ are induced by $U\to V$ and $W\to V$. Under this equivalence, the slice projection $P/H_Z\to P$ is the localization morphism induced by the three maps $U\to X$, $V\to S$, and $W\to Y$ and their commutativity.

proof.text: Work with small sites in [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathcal C$ for the triple site of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] and $\mathcal C_Z$ for the triple site for $U\to V\leftarrow W$. An object of $\mathcal C/Z$ is a triple $(A\to B\leftarrow D)$ with maps $a:A\to U$, $b:B\to V$, $d:D\to W$ such that the two squares commute. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], applied separately to $U\to X$, $V\to S$, $W\to Y$, these are precisely objects $A\in U_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $B\in V_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $D\in W_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with arrows $A\to B\leftarrow D$ over the two arrows of $Z$. The same commuting diagrams define their morphisms. Forgetting or adjoining the composites to $X,S,Y$ gives mutually inverse equivalences of these categories; their unit and counit are the identity on the underlying schemes and arrows. No arrow $U\to V$ or $W\to V$ is being assumed etale.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), site realization of diagram (1.a); small etale localization: Stacks sites.tex Section 00XZ and the cited etale-site equivalence

proof.text: Identify the topologies under step 1. For types (a) and (b) of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], the unchanged middle and opposite components stay unchanged over $Z$, and the covering of $A$, respectively $D$, is the same jointly surjective etale family on either side. For type (c), a middle arrow $B'\to B$ and a factorization $A\to B'$ give the singleton arrow $(A\to B'\leftarrow D\times_B B')\to(A\to B\leftarrow D)$; the map $B'\to V$ is the composite through $B$, and the map of its last component to $W$ is the composite through $D$. This is exactly type (c) on the relative triple site, in both directions. In the localized topology [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] all the arrows into an object over $Z$ acquire their maps to $Z$ by composition. Lifting the generating families therefore commutes with pullback and composition: the targets already map to $Z$ and their sources have the unique induced maps. Close the generators under isomorphisms, pullback and composition and apply [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition]. The resulting covering sieves agree, so step 1 is an equivalence of sites.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.1(a)-(c) and 1.10(b); generated-topology criterion: Stacks Tag 00ZC (lemma-site-gives-topology)

proof.text: By [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] applied to $U\to V$ and $W\to V$, put $Q=U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{V_{\mathrm{Et}}}W_{\mathrm{Et}}=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_Z)$. The small etale sites have finite limits [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; their base-change site functors preserve them and coverings, as in the original triple construction. Reindexing a presheaf through the equivalence of step 1, and its inverse, preserves the sheaf matching and gluing conditions because of step 2. It gives inverse equivalences $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/Z)\simeq Q$, with componentwise unit and counit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] to the small site $\mathcal C$ and the object $Z$. Its equivalence $E_Z:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/Z)\simeq P/H_Z$, composed with the preceding equivalence, gives the asserted equivalence of topoi. This uses the sheafified representable $H_Z$, without assuming that $h_Z$ is a sheaf.

Identify the projection under $E_Z$. The inverse image of the slice projection is $\pi^{-1}F=(F\times H_Z\to H_Z)$. The explicit quasi-inverse $R_Z$ in [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] evaluates this object at $(T\xrightarrow{a}Z)$ as the fibre of $F(T)\times H_Z(T)\to H_Z(T)$ over $\eta_T(a)$. The maps $s\mapsto(s,\eta_T(a))$ and $(s,\eta_T(a))\mapsto s$ are inverse bijections, natural under restrictions and in $F$. Thus $R_Z\pi^{-1}F(T,a)=F(T)$. This is exactly $j_Z^{-1}F$, restriction along $\mathcal C/Z\to\mathcal C$ in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Hence the constructed equivalence intertwines $\pi$ with the site-localization morphism $j_Z$, including its inverse image, rather than just giving an abstract equivalence of categories.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), localization map (1.c); Stacks Tag 00Y1 (fibre quasi-inverse) and Definition 00Y0

proof.text: It remains to identify $j_Z$ with the morphism induced by the three scheme maps. Define $b:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C/Z$ by $T\mapsto(T\times Z\to Z)$, with componentwise pullback. For $T=(A\to B\leftarrow D)$, its image in $\mathcal C_Z$ is $(A\times_X U\to B\times_S V\leftarrow D\times_Y W)$. The maps to the middle component use both commutative squares of $Z$. The final triple maps to $Z$ as its identity, and componentwise pullbacks are preserved, so $b$ preserves finite limits. Each type-(a), (b), or (c) generating family maps to its pullback along $T\times Z\to T$, hence covers; this persists under compositions. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], $b$ defines a geometric morphism $t:Q\to P$ with direct image $(t_*G)(T)=G(T\times Z\to Z)$. All these sites are small in the universes fixed in step 1.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.9 and 1.10(b), site model for the functoriality map; Stacks Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism)

proof.text: The functor $b$ is the componentwise base-change functor for $U\to X$, $V\to S$, $W\to Y$. More explicitly it sends $k_1(A)=(A\to S\leftarrow Y)$ to $k'_1(A\times_X U)=(A\times_X U\to V\leftarrow W)$, and $k_2(D)=(X\to S\leftarrow D)$ to $k'_2(D\times_Y W)$. For a middle object $B\in S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, the middle triple $(X\times_S B\to B\leftarrow Y\times_S B)$ is sent to the middle triple over $B\times_S V$; here $U\times_V(B\times_S V)=U\times_S B$, and similarly for $W$. Its two structural arrows to $k_1(X\times_S B)$ and $k_2(Y\times_S B)$ are carried to those same structural arrows over $V$. Apply the explicit inverse-image formula of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] with the identity lift of $P$ (and likewise of $Q$). For this middle triple its last map to the fibre-product base is the identity, so the first structural arrow becomes an isomorphism and the second, after this identification, is the mate of the canonical $2$-morphism. This recovers the mate from the cited statement, not from its proof. Thus the projection functors and their $2$-morphism commute with $b$. The composition isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] identify the corresponding geometric morphisms. By the uniqueness clause of the oriented-product universal property, $t$ is precisely the morphism induced by the three scheme maps and their commutativity.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.3, Theorem 1.4, 1.9 and 1.10(b); explicit check of the projections and the mate of tau

proof.text: Finally $t_*$ is right adjoint to the restriction $j_Z^{-1}$. This can be checked without any density assertion: given $\alpha:j_Z^{-1}F\to G$, define $F(T)\to G(T\times Z\to Z)$ by restricting a section to $T\times Z$ and then applying $\alpha$ at that object. Conversely, from $\beta:F\to t_*G$ and an object $(T,a)$ over $Z$, apply $\beta_T$ and restrict along the arrow $(\mathrm{id}_T,a):(T,a)\to(T\times Z,\mathrm{pr}_Z)$. Naturality and $\mathrm{pr}_T(\mathrm{id}_T,a)=\mathrm{id}_T$ show that these operations are inverse; they are natural in both sheaves. Restriction is $j_Z^{-1}$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], so this adjunction identifies $t$ with $j_Z$. Combining with step 4 shows that the equivalence of step 3 is over $P$ and identifies the slice projection with the specified localization morphism, as required.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), map (1.c); elementary restriction/right-adjoint calculation on the localized site

proof_origin.place: Exposé XI 1.10(b), expanding the assertion that (1.b) is an equivalence by its triple-site presentation; auxiliary localization equivalence is Stacks 00Y1.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q38-4f915e320 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item's seven steps, every cited node's statement in full, ILO Travaux de Gabber XI 1.9–1.10(b) on printed pp. 175–176 (diagram 1.a, the equivalence m in (1.b), the localization arrow (1.c)), and the blueprint proof of lem-trf-local-term-locality in main-20261015. There are no new nodes. The statement matches the source and is not weakened. The source only asserts that m is an equivalence; the split proves it. Step 1 is correct: an object over Z is the same as an arrow A→U×_V B, and the componentwise etale-site localization applies because U, V, W are etale over X, S, Y. Step 2 is correct: in both sites the last component of a type-(c) cover is D×_B B'. Its terse claim that lifting commutes with pullback holds because the generating covers are stable under pullback up to isomorphism (pullbacks are componentwise), so every cover is a composite of generators whose intermediate objects already lie over Z. Step 3 is correct: Stacks 00Y1 is used without assuming subcanonicity, which matters because the triple site is not subcanonical. Steps 4 to 7 are correct: the fibre over eta(a) is F(T); the functor T↦T×Z preserves finite limits and covers; the canonical 2-morphism is recovered from the cited inverse-image formula, not from that node's proof; and I checked both round trips of the adjunction through the projection and diagonal identities, so t is j_Z. Small cases checked: the final triple, an empty component, a type-(c) map with B'=B, and h_Z not a sheaf. I found no duplicate in the DAG; the parent lem-trf-oriented-affine-slice-site is strictly larger. There is no cycle and the unit route is unchanged. I accept the three tool_uses, which the worker recorded itself: etale-site-localization-open (already proved in slopmaster2), and localized-sheaves-over-representable and left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor, generic site lemmas that the trace-formula unit lacks. The left-exact one is already a recorded tool of lem-trf-oriented-product-universal in the same unit. No changes made.
